content: The following treatment regimens will be excluded from the current analysis: 1. Short regimens that do not include bedaquiline and do not align with the 2020 World Health Organization (WHO) recommendations. Patients receiving these regimens will not be included in comparative analyses, as bedaquiline is considered one of the most effective drugs for treating multidrug-resistant or rifampin-resistant tuberculosis (MDR/RR-TB). 2. Short-course regimens that include both bedaquiline and an injectable antibiotic. Patients who initially received injectable antibiotics before transitioning to a bedaquiline-containing regimen will also be excluded from comparative analyses, as these regimens do not comply with the 2020 WHO guidelines. Note: Regimens lasting 12 months are defined as any treatment duration up to 365 days. The term 9–12 months is used in the 2020 WHO consolidated treatment guidelines. The public call for data is expected to significantly contribute to the comparator regimens. Fluoroquinolone antibiotics, such as levofloxacin or moxifloxacin, are part of the standardized treatment for MDR/RR-TB according to the 2019 WHO guidelines and the 2020 consolidated guidelines. To align with WHO recommendations, a fluoroquinolone must be included in the regimen unless resistance to fluoroquinolones has been demonstrated. In the primary analysis, some individuals may discontinue treatment early due to death, loss to follow-up, or treatment failure. Toxicity may also necessitate early dose reductions of certain drugs, such as linezolid. Eligibility for Inclusion in the Evidence Review The datasets included in this review were identified by the WHO Global TB Program in 2021 following a public call for data. These datasets include clinical trials and patient cohorts treated for MDR/RR-TB between the previous WHO Guideline Development Group meeting in April 2017 and December 2021. Criteria for Dataset Inclusion: 1. Data must come from clinical trials (with or without a comparator group) or cohorts of patients treated for MDR/RR-TB in a programmatic setting. 2. At least 25 patients must have completed treatment, with an assigned end-of-treatment outcome. 3. Included patients must have MDR/RR-TB. 4. The dataset must provide sufficient information to determine the composition and duration of treatment regimens and assign treatment outcomes for most participants. 5. Patients must have been treated with an intervention or comparator regimen relevant to this review. Criteria for Patient Inclusion: 1. Patients must have bacteriologically confirmed Mycobacterium tuberculosis (via PCR or culture). 2. Rifampin resistance (with or without isoniazid resistance) must be confirmed by phenotypic or genotypic drug susceptibility testing within 365 days prior to treatment initiation, or probable rifampin resistance must be documented. 3. Treatment regimen composition and duration must be clearly defined. 4. For PICO questions involving fluoroquinolone status, baseline fluoroquinolone resistance must be documented. Additional eligibility criteria specific to included regimens are described in the relevant sections below. Outcomes to Be Analyzed The WHO-directed PICO questions identify the following treatment outcomes: (a) Cured (b) Treatment completed (c) Treatment failed (d) Death (e) Lost to follow-up (f) Adverse events (including drug-drug interactions in HIV-infected patients) (g) Amplification (acquisition) of drug resistance Outcome Definitions: Where possible, outcome definitions will follow the standardized guidelines for MDR-TB adopted by WHO in November 2020. In comparative analyses, cure and treatment completed will be combined as treatment success. Sustained treatment success will be defined as no documented relapse by the date of censoring, in accordance with WHO 2020 definitions. Statistical Analysis Plan Comparative analyses will be conducted within individual studies and across multiple studies. Outcomes will be presented as unadjusted and adjusted risk ratios. Adjusted risk ratios will be calculated using log-binomial generalized linear regression, with confounders adjusted using inverse probability propensity score weighting. If convergence issues arise, Poisson regression with robust variance estimation or logistic regression for odds ratios will be used. Missing Data: For adjusted risk ratio calculations, multiple imputation by chained equations will be used to account for missing data in potential confounders when the proportion of missing values is less than 45%. At least 20 iterations will be performed to impute missing values, and results will be compared to complete case analysis. Missing drug susceptibility test results will be assumed to indicate susceptibility, except for rifampin, where evidence of resistance is required. Sensitivity Analyses Additional sensitivity analyses will assess the impact of eligibility criteria and follow-up times on outcomes. These include: Follow-up to 12 months for regimens lasting no more than 12 months. Follow-up to 18 months for regimens lasting no more than 18 months. Modeling bestand worst-case scenarios for mortality in cohorts with incomplete follow-up data. Stratification Effect estimates will be stratified by the following characteristics, where possible: 1. Fluoroquinolone resistance status 2. Smear positivity 3. Presence of cavitation on chest X-ray 4. HIV status 5. Baseline culture status 6. Age (0–14 years vs. 15 years and above) 7. Smoking status 8. However, comparisons between trials may be influenced by differences in participant characteristics, programmatic settings, standards of care, and timing of diagnosis. Incomplete data may also pose limitations in some datasets. Description of Included Cohorts The included cohorts consist of clinical trials and programmatic datasets, such as the TB-PRACTECAL trial, the South African TB Program 2019 cohort, and the 2021 WHO Individual Patient Data (IPD) dataset. These cohorts include patients with microbiologically confirmed MDR/RR-TB treated with various regimens, including shorter all-oral regimens and longer regimens containing bedaquiline and linezolid. TB-PRACTECAL Trial The TB-PRACTECAL trial was a multi-center, open-label, randomized controlled Phase 2/3 trial evaluating short-course (24-week) all-oral regimens containing bedaquiline and pretomanid for the treatment of pulmonary MDR/RR-TB. The trial was terminated early in March 2021 due to evidence favoring the bedaquiline, pretomanid, linezolid, and moxifloxacin (BPaLM) regimen over the standard of care. The primary outcome was the percentage of participants with an unfavorable outcome (death, treatment failure, recurrence, or loss to follow-up) at 72 weeks post-randomization. Analytical Considerations The early termination of the TB-PRACTECAL trial reduced the power to detect differences between treatment arms. Comparator regimens also changed over time, potentially affecting the proportion of unsuccessful outcomes in the comparator group. Sensitivity analyses will explore these factors.
